coverageSpotVerification.detail: coverage-manifest.json maps all 58 in-scope suite-required assertions (M1 7, M2 22, M3 7, M4 5, M5 6, M6 5, M8 6) with no omissions, and scripts/coverage.mjs derives the list from assertions.json itself rather than from a hand-written set. I read the source of every mapped test (scripts/acceptance.mjs and scripts/suite-m2..m8.mjs) and traced the 29 sampled ids to concrete observations; each mapped test really exercises its assertion’s observable, several at both the API and the UI layer (e.g. follow-projection checks the Following/Global split through the query layer, pagination-scroll-no-gaps checks 20-per-page plus set-equality of ids, repost-attribution-and-self checks the rendered attribution node and that profileStats are unchanged). I re-ran all seven suites myself and every one passed independently. The only wording gap found is defect d-05 (m1-a03 mapped to the profile-edit path rather than onboarding); I verified the assertion holds on the onboarding path too, so the mapping is honest, not dishonest.

defects.summary: Typing-indicator expiry is coupled to typing rate and server write backlog: src/chat.tsx fires one unthrottled chat.setTyping mutation on every keystroke, and snapback/chat.q:182 stamps expiresAt = server-processing-time + 3500 ms, so the deadline is set by the last write to drain rather than the last keystroke. Measured 3.82 s after a 10-character burst but 4.885–4.913 s after the frozen harness’s 45-character/25 ms cadence, and over the brief’s 5 s ceiling on 6/6 harness attempts across two independent runs. It also means one server write per keystroke per typing user.
defects.evidence: trace.md §5 (g-typing.mjs, g-typing-seq.mjs, g-typing-harnesslike.mjs measurement tables); grading/receipts/all-choreo.jsonl and grading/receipts/m3-choreo.jsonl; src/chat.tsx:30 (Composer onChangeText), snapback/chat.q:180-182

defects.summary: scripts/replay.mjs cannot be re-run against an already-replayed backend with a fresh REPLAY_STATE: the first profile-set line reuses a write id derived deterministically from the log hash but mints a new asset, so the server refuses with E_ID_REUSED and the script dies on an unhandled throw with a raw stack trace instead of a diagnostic pointing at the journal. README documents that a fresh store needs fresh progress, but the M6 conformance deliverable is the one a grader re-runs "from a clean checkout".
defects.evidence: trace.md §3.7 — REPLAY_STATE=grading/replay-dev node scripts/replay.mjs instrument/fixtures/sample-50.log; scripts/replay.mjs:14

defects.summary: scripts/acceptance.mjs rewrites evidence/suite-status.json with only the milestone just run, so after any single-milestone acceptance run the file the choreography harness requires (--suite-status, keyed by every selected segment) is incomplete. The complete file is only reassembled by scripts/finalize.mjs, which is not part of the documented per-milestone loop; I had to build my own suite-status to drive the harness.

scripts/custom-client-demo.mjs — the M6 deliverable — hardcodes the fixture password as its CLIQUE_PASSWORD default, which is exactly what its own API.md tells third-party developers never to ship ("Never ship fixture credentials in a public deployment"). No end-user password is stored reversibly anywhere (m1-a13 passes); this is a test-fixture credential in a shipped example.

The suite test mapped to m1-a03 ("signing up with a duplicate handle is rejected with a visible error") exercises handle uniqueness on the profile-edit screen rather than the onboarding step where a signing-up user first chooses a handle. The mapping is still honest — I confirmed independently that onboarding with handle "alice" is refused HANDLE_TAKEN — but the test is one screen away from the assertion’s wording.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("M1–M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap") and the 90 anchor ("every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts"), interpolated toward 90.
O1.justification: 100 of the 119 frozen assertions pass under independent execution (84%): M1 13/13, M2 27/27, M3 14/15, M4 12/12, M5 12/12, M6 6/13, M7 0/9, M8 16/18. M1–M6 and M8 are all substantively solid — every suite-required and web-choreography assertion passes except one — so this sits well above the 60 anchor. It cannot reach 90 for two reasons the anchor names directly: the platform-proof artifacts do not exist (no iOS-simulator artifact for M6 or M8, so m6-a01..a07 and m8-a17/a18 are unevidenced), and M7 is not-run and stays in the denominator per the applicability rule. The single outright failure is m3-a07 (typing-indicator expiry, defect d-01).

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ("a few medium defects off the happy path") and the 90 anchor ("only cosmetic nits"), interpolated toward 90.
O2.justification: One major defect (d-01: per-keystroke unthrottled typing writes making a brief-specified 5 s bound rate- and load-dependent — on the happy path, though its blast radius is a ~100 ms overshoot on an ephemeral indicator; it overlaps checklist item m3-a07, and I weighted it accordingly), two minor re-runnability/DX defects (d-02, d-03), two cosmetic (d-04, d-05). No crash, no wrong data, no broken flow, and no authorization leak: 21 beyond-checklist trust-boundary probes all behaved correctly (non-member chat reads return empty result sets rather than content, cross-user edit/delete refuse NOT_AUTHOR, private-chat assets 404 for outsiders and 401 unauthenticated, the effects endpoint refuses a user token, view-once assets serve exactly once per recipient then 410). Two rounds of independent re-execution of every suite and the whole choreography turned up nothing beyond the above.

O4.anchorsCited: Above the 30 anchor ("cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app") but far below the 60 anchor ("reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush"), both of which the rubric reads over the native proof.
O4.justification: O4 scores from the harness’s simulator artifacts, and there are none: simulator.md’s three required files are absent, and both the builder’s and my own choreography receipts carry ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 as {"pass":null,"status":"not-recorded"}. The brief is explicit that missing evidence leaves the native/O4 proof absent rather than passing it, so nothing native can be credited — no cold-start reads, no cold-offline search, no view-once non-caching, no durable-queue-across-restart. What lifts this above the failure anchor is the second half of O4’s definition, honesty of the gap between claim and guarantee, where the lane is exact: native-artifacts.json lists only Hermes exports, README states "Native simulation is not claimed by an export" and that Expo Go’s fallback "does not claim durable native offline support", and the harness receipt records the non-result rather than a fabricated pass. The web-carrier offline evidence that does exist is real and correct in my own runs (M6 ordered offline queue flush 681.8 ms, M5 warm-offline search, M8 dual-offline convergence with no loss or duplicates and receipts reaching read, and a durable outbox surviving a page reload on the production web export), but it is the web carrier, not the artifact this dimension reads.

O5.bandRationale: First-match evaluation. Band 0 does not fire: I independently re-verified the invariant manifest on a private copy of the scale instance and it conforms exactly — 100 015 messages, 50 228 posts, 1 008 profiles, and every named O5 fixture exact (u0900 900 followers / 200 posts, u0500 500 follows / 100 conversations, u0005 5 follows, u0901 5 follows, g0001 50 members / 10 000 messages) — and the lane’s own harness-validated checkpoints at 10%, 50% and final all passed 24/24; the replay’s recorded action clock was 668 s (verification to +708 s) against the environment’s 4-hour per-milestone safety limit standing in for the uninstantiated cap, i.e. ~4.6%, so the cap was not exhausted. Band 30 does not fire: across 16 grader-run probes (k=20 after 3 warm-ups, sequential, 30 s timeout) there were zero timeouts, errors or OOMs, and every evaluable degradation rule passes — deep paging page 50/page 1 = 0.88×, 500-follow vs 5-follow Following feed = 1.13×, celebrity-follower read path = 0.88×, celebrity write path = 0.51× (fan-out is not on the write path), global search full/10% = 0.97–1.16×, full inbox paging for the 100-conversation probe user 6.1 ms, and Insights is served from maintained read models (snapback/insights.q) rather than client-side paging, at 1.6–1.7 ms p95. Band 60 does not fire: the frozen instrument never instantiated the absolute p95 ceiling table (it still reads "pilot-calibrated"), so no ceiling is exceeded, and replay used far under 80% of its cap. Band 90 cannot fire: its condition requires a positive determination that every probe’s observed ceiling utilization is <=50%, and with no ceilings instantiated that utilization is not computable. First match after 0/30/60/90 is therefore 75. Two judgement calls are recorded in trace.md §10: (a) the global-search mid-curve sub-rule — the lane’s 50% checkpoint p95 sits 0.12–0.62 ms above the straight line between the 10% and full-corpus points for all three actors, which I read as measurement noise on 1.7–2.8 ms samples taken in a different process on a machine at load average 14–24, not the "superlinear blow-up" the rule targets, since the full-corpus value is at or below the 10% value for two of three actors; (b) the M8 Insights and Trending mid-curve rules are not evaluable at all, because the lane backfilled the M8 read models onto the scale instance only after the replay finished, so no 10%/50% Insights or Trending measurements exist. I treated (b) as unevaluated rather than failed.

notes: N=1 calibration run, not claim-eligible. Three prescribed deviations from the frozen protocol: (1) no holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped, wave.probeSetSha256 is the sentinel "none-uncommitted", and probeResults is empty — no probes were invented; because O3 is scored from the wave’s secret rotated probes only, its single permitted input does not exist and O3 records null even though applicability.json makes it applicable (M6 green, M1–M5 attempted).
